entries.snippet: The US Food and Drug Administration says Ozempic, Wegovy, and other weight-loss drugs must have labels about the condition, known as NAION.

entries.title: Should you trust new AI agents with your money and data?

entries.title: Testing the new generation of AI-enabled fire-extinguishing drones
entries.snippet: Drone makers are testing new, big drones that can deliver water or fire retardant with AI assistance. Aspen, Colorado is the first place trying them out. Cool and expensive? Yes. Effective? TBD.

entries.title: U.S. boycotts U.N. human rights review for second year running
entries.snippet: The U.S. has skipped a key U.N. human rights review for the second year running. Rights groups warn the absence risks undermining global accountability.

entries.title: Americans across the economic spectrum feel a 'panic' about finances, author says
entries.snippet: Mona Chalabi spent five years following Americans living paycheck to paycheck, as well as those earning top wages. Her new book, Ten Lives, explores why financial security can feel so elusive.

entries.title: Gas prices dip below $4 but inflation remains stubbornly high
entries.snippet: Gasoline prices fell below $4 a gallon Tuesday for the first time in three months — but the overall cost of living remains stubbornly high.

entries.title: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent
entries.snippet: Little is known about her except that she's reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae, but Korea's spy agency says she's likely her father's heir.

entries.title: Indonesia's VP offers resignation as questions mount over his eligibility
entries.snippet: His resignation offer comes amid a widening political rift between Prabowo and Widodo and a separate investigation into allegations that senior police officials wiretapped the president.

entries.title: The average cost for a new vehicle in the U.S. hits a record high: over $51,000
entries.snippet: Vehicle transaction prices are up to a new record high, according to the Kelley Blue Book — and some buyers are extending their car loans to finance them.

entries.snippet: Five countries have backed a plan to double the number of homes with rooftop solar panels worldwide by 2030, as U.N. climate talks in Turkey focus on expanding access to electricity and transitioning away from fossil fuels.

entries.title: California voters reject tax on net worth of billionaires
entries.snippet: The measure would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion.

entries.title: British comedian and children's author David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct

entries.title: Former Malaysian leader Najib Razak returns home under royal pardon, but faces a separate 15-year prison sentence
entries.snippet: Najib Razak has left prison under a royal pardon, prompting a minister to resign in protest. Malaysia's former leader still faces a separate 15-year sentence over the corruption scandal that brought him down.

entries.title: British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
entries.snippet: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

entries.title: UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
entries.snippet: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

entries.title: Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
entries.snippet: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

entries.title: Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
entries.snippet: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

entries.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
entries.snippet: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.

entries.title: Poland: Krakow shooting suspect 'fascinated' by Norwegian mass murder Anders Breivik, says justice minister
entries.snippet: The 24-year old suspect was found to have read a significant amount of material about Breivik and other far-right figures. Speculation over his motives have prompted a bitter political feud in Warsaw.

entries.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
entries.snippet: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.

entries.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
entries.snippet: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

entries.title: Pope Leo vs. Javier Milei: How political is the pope?
entries.snippet: Pope Leo XIV's tour of South America has drawn huge crowds — and a measure of political controversy. Perceived criticism of Argentina's leader, and earlier rebukes of Donald Trump, offer a glimpse into papacy politics.

entries.title: Japan watches for signs of change in Trump's foreign policy priorities
entries.snippet: Tokyo fears the drubbing US President Donald Trump suffered in last week's midterm election may push him to pursue a diplomatic quick win at the expense of Washington's allies in the Indo-Pacific.

entries.title: Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
entries.snippet: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.

entries.title: India: Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' released
entries.snippet: The book goes through the Italian-born matriarch's journey with one of India's most politically influential families. It has already garnered political controversy, with the ruling BJP accusing her of "whitewashing."

entries.title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion
entries.snippet: Felix Nmecha's "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.

entries.title: Spain: Police officer killed in Oviedo after neighborhood dispute escalates with explosion
entries.snippet: After security services responded to a shooting, a bomb found in a backpack nearby detonated before it could be defused.

entries.title: Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
entries.snippet: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.

entries.title: DR Congo: 66 soldiers sentenced to death for 'cowardice' in conflict with FRN rebels
entries.snippet: Dozens of defendants were put on trial over accusations that they abandoned their posts and refused to follow direct orders.

entries.title: Germany news: Ilse Aigner meets parties at Bundestag
entries.snippet: Ilse Aigner said she wouldn't meet with the far-right AfD. Meanwhile, Chancellor Merz is set to host Hungarian Prime Minister Magyar. DW has more.

entries.title: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need
